mcq.explanation: A Docker image is a read-only template for creating containers: stacked filesystem layers plus metadata such as the default command. A container adds a writable layer on top.
mcq.distractors: An image is not a VM, a Git branch or a DNS record; containers share the host kernel instead of booting their own OS.

mcq.explanation: `docker build` builds an image from a Dockerfile and a build context, e.g. `docker build -t myapp:1.0 .`.
mcq.distractors: `docker start` starts an existing container, `docker logs` shows output and `docker exec` runs a command in a running container.

mcq.explanation: `FROM` sets the base image and must be the first instruction (only `ARG` may come before it), e.g. `FROM nginx:alpine`.
mcq.distractors: `COPY` adds files, `CMD` sets the default command and `EXPOSE` documents a port.

mcq.explanation: `COPY` copies files from the build context into the image, e.g. `COPY index.html /usr/share/nginx/html/`.
mcq.distractors: `USER` sets the runtime user, `WORKDIR` sets the working directory and `RUN` executes a command at build time.

mcq.explanation: `docker ps` lists running containers; add `-a` to include stopped ones.
mcq.distractors: `docker images` lists images, `docker build` builds and `docker pull` downloads images.

mcq.explanation: `-p 8080:80` maps host port 8080 to container port 80; the format is `HOST:CONTAINER`, so you browse to localhost:8080.
mcq.distractors: The order is host first, container second, and `-p` publishes ports, not volumes (that is `-v`).

mcq.explanation: `docker logs` shows a container's standard output and error streams, e.g. `docker logs -f web`.
mcq.distractors: Registry credentials are in Docker's config, Git history comes from `git log` and Docker never shows kernel source.

mcq.explanation: `docker exec` executes a command inside a running container, e.g. `docker exec -it web sh`.
mcq.distractors: `docker save` exports an image to a tar file, `docker tag` names an image and `docker push` uploads it.

mcq.explanation: .dockerignore is used to exclude paths from the build context (e.g. `.git`, `node_modules`, `.env`), making builds faster and keeping secrets out of images.
mcq.distractors: It does not affect networking, runtime errors or what `docker ps` shows.

mcq.explanation: `CMD` defines the default command a container runs, which can be overridden by arguments to `docker run`.
mcq.distractors: `LABEL` adds metadata, `ARG` defines build-time variables and `EXPOSE` documents ports.

# .dockerignore
.git
*.log
.env
node_modules
Dockerfile
.dockerignore

# Dockerfile
FROM nginx:alpine
ARG APP_VERSION=1.0
ENV APP_ENV=production \
    APP_VERSION=${APP_VERSION}
WORKDIR /usr/share/nginx/html
COPY index.html .
CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"]

# rebuild and run
docker build --build-arg APP_VERSION=1.1 -t my-html:1.1 .
docker run -d --name site2 -p 8081:80 my-html:1.1
docker exec site2 printenv APP_ENV APP_VERSION   # production / 1.1
docker run --rm -e APP_ENV=staging my-html:1.1 printenv APP_ENV   # override at runtime -> staging

# Purpose of each addition
# .dockerignore: excludes files from the build context, so builds are faster and secrets such as .env or the .git history never end up in the image.
# ARG: a build-time variable (set with --build-arg); it is not available in the running container unless copied into ENV.
# ENV: sets an environment variable baked into the image and visible to the running process; it can be overridden with docker run -e.
labs.explanation: Tests two build-time features: shrinking and securing the build context with .dockerignore, and configuring the image with environment variables. Verify the variable inside the running container (`docker exec ... printenv`), and that the explanation distinguishes ARG (build time only) from ENV (persists into the container, overridable with `-e`). Never put real secrets in ENV or ARG, since they are visible in the image history.
